sometime the server deletion fails mid-run: the server would then appear as already stopped (status unknown) and subsequent stop would skip deletion attempt, but infrastructure state is left inconsistent as over resources were not properly updated (eg. data disk config or such)

Merge pull request #324 from PierreBeucher/gcp-provisioning-enhancements

Gcp provisioning enhancements

fix: ensure data disk is always attached to Linode

Pulumi idempotence was broken causing data disk to be detached on seconds runs. When deployment failed for X reason and retried, disk was detached from instance.

Before:
1. on first pulumi attached disk properly on instanceConfig. As dataVolume was created AFTER desiredInstanceConfig, it was attached to this config by default. desiredInstanceConfig is first created with no data disk, but data volume creation afterward atached it peroperly.
2. On second run, desiredInstanceConfig was updated to use the default config which lacked data disk config. Since data volume wasn't updated afterward, it as then missing from desired instance config.

Now we ensure dataVolume is always set as a device on desiredInstanceConfig

fix: reinforce check for NVIDIA installer on container setup

fix: force NVIDIA Container Toolkit version to 1.17.8-1 to avoid black screen issues with 1.18.x and Container Device Interface

In short: NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.18.x is now using Container Device Interface (CDI) instead of "legacy" behavior to mount devices in container (/dev/nvidia*, /dev/dri/*, etc.), causing some (lots of?) games to crash on startup or run with sound only and a black screen

with PROTON_LOG=1 %command% set as custom commands symptom are errors related to Vulkan and swapchain like "1760.863:0134:0194:err:vkd3d-proton:dxgi_vk_swap_chain_recreate_swapchain_in_present_task: Failed to create swapchain, vr -13." or other code "13" related error

Rolling back to 1.17.x (using legacy behavior) seems to fix the issue for now.

See https://discord.com/channels/1349805499952005150/1467859554388807804 on public Discord

feat(aws): add --create-vpc option to provision a dedicated VPC

Add a --create-vpc flag (and matching interactive wizard prompt) that
creates a full public networking stack before the EC2 instance:

- VPC (10.0.0.0/16, DNS enabled)
- Internet Gateway
- One public subnet per availability zone (10.0.N.0/24), each with
  mapPublicIpOnLaunch enabled, so spot instances can be scheduled in
  whichever AZ has capacity
- Route table with a default route to the IGW, associated to every subnet

If --zone is specified the instance uses that AZ's subnet; otherwise the
first available subnet is used and AWS picks the AZ.

The createVpc flag is persisted in instance state and passed through to
Pulumi on every subsequent provision so the VPC lifecycle is fully
managed alongside the instance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(aws): enable IPv6 for created VPC

Assign an Amazon-provided IPv6 /56 block to the VPC and carve a /64 per
subnet. Add a ::/0 route to the IGW so instances get a routable IPv6
address without any extra configuration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Extract VPC creation into a CloudyPadVpc ComponentResource to encapsulate networking concerns
- Fix AZ stability: use {region}a instead of subnets[0] so repeated Pulumi runs always target the same AZ, keeping EBS volumes and instances co-located
- CLI flag renamed --create-vpc -> --dedicated-vpc

fix: move PNPM_HOME to /usr/local/share/pnpm so non-root users can execute cloudypad

The cloudypad binary is installed by the root user into the default
PNPM_HOME of $HOME/.local/share/pnpm. Linux sets /root to mode 700, so
any non-root user that tries to traverse into it receives "Permission
denied" even if the binary itself were world-executable.

cloudypad.sh works by pulling the base image then building a thin wrapper
on top that adds a user matching the host UID/GID. That wrapper user is
non-root, so when Docker resolves the "cloudypad" ENTRYPOINT through PATH
it immediately hits the /root traversal block.

/usr/local/share/pnpm has mode 755 and is traversable by all users,
making it the appropriate location for a system-wide install in an image
where the executing user is determined at runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
